The applicants seeks quashment of FIR in Crime No.
293/2023 registered with Nardana Police Station, Nardana, Tq.
Shindkheda, Dist. Dhule for offences punishable under sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506 r/w. 34 of IPC as well as consequential proceeding in Regular Criminal Case No.186/2023 pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class, Shindkheda.
2. Investigation was set in motion on the basis of information given by respondent no.2, alleging that on 2.2.2015 she was married with applicant no.1.
Couple is blessed with a daughter in the year 2016.
It is alleged that she was treated well for initial six months.
Lateron, her in-laws ill- treated her alleging that her father failed to perform marriage  3 cran 4233.23.odt as per their expectations and informant has no cooking skills.
It is alleged that after delivery, when she returned to matrimonial home with baby, she was teased that girl is born.
Thereafter, in-laws raised demand of Rs.10.00 Lakh for starting new business of her husband.

It is further alleged that in the year 2021, husband filed proceedings for divorce and driven Vishal Eknath Deore And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 27 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112961890/

Per contra, Mr. Lomte, learned APP appearing for respondent no.1/State and Mr.Sant, learned advocate appearing for respondent no.2 vehemently opposed prayers in the application.
They would submit that informant was consistently teased by all applicants.
Firstly, for the reason that marriage was not performed as per their expectations and secondly as informant delivered a girl child.

8. Having considered submissions advanced by learned advocates appearing for respective parties and on perusal of allegations in FIR coupled with material collected during investigation, it is evident that informant married in the year  5 cran 4233.23.odt 2015.
She delivered a girl child on 19.5.2016.

During this period, only allegation is that, in-laws abused her or teased for the reason that she has no skills of cooking or at the marriage ceremony her father failed to meet expectations of in-laws.
9. The second part of allegations is after return to matrimonial home on delivery of child, here allegation is that in-laws teased her that she could not deliver a male child.
Thereafter, one mere allegation is employed that demand was raised to bring Rs.10.00 Lakhs for the business of husband.
10. Last part of the FIR states about filing of divorce petition.
Apparently, allegations in FIR are vague, unspecific and general in nature.
No role is attributed against individual applicant.

As rightly pointed out by Mr. Patil, applicant is residing at her Vishal Eknath Deore And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 27 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112961890/

11. Evidently, all allegations in the FIR are regarding acts of applicants prior to 2020.
Even, assuming that allegations are true and correct, those are short to make out offence under section 498-A of the IPC.

It can be observed that when FIR is  6 cran 4233.23.odt lodged beyond three years of date of last offence, cognizance cannot be taken in light of section 468 of the Criminal Procedure Code as maximum punishment provided for offence under section 498-A is three years.

12. In the aforesaid background, reference can be given to the observations of the Supreme Court of India in case of Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and Others Versus State of Bihar and Others (2022) 6 SCC 599 wherein it has been observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in paragraph Nos.17 that -  17.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and Others Versus State of Bihar and Others (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The above-mentioned decisions clearly  demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances  expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC  and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of  the husband in matrimonial disputes, without  analyzing the long term ramifications of a trial on the  complainant as well as the accused.

It is further  manifest from the said judgments that false implication  by way of general omnibus allegations made in the  course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would  result in misuse of the process of law.

Therefore, this  court by way of its judgments has warned the courts  from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the  husband when no prima facie case is made out against Vishal Eknath Deore And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 27 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112961890/
5  them."

sentences.text: It is a matter of common knowledge that  unfortunately matrimonial litigation is rapidly  increasing in our country.
All the courts in our country  including this Court are flooded with matrimonial  cases.
This clearly demonstrates discontent and unrest  in the family life of a large number of people of the  society.
32. It is a matter of common experience that most of these  complaints under section 498-A IPC are filed in the  heat of the moment over trivial issues without proper  deliberations.
We come across a large number of such  complaints which are not even bona fide and are filed  with oblique motive.
At the same time, rapid increase  in the number of genuine cases of dowry harassment  are also a matter of serious concern.

34. Unfortunately, at the time of filing of the complaint  the implications and consequences are not properly  visualized by the complainant that such complaint can  lead to insurmountable harassment, agony and pain to  the complainant, accused and his close relations."
14. In the case of Geeta Mehrotra and Another Versus State of Uttar Pradesh and Another (2012) 10 SCC 74, Hon'ble Supreme Court observed in para no. 25 that-  25.

sentences.text:
It is the well settled principle laid  down in cases too numerous to mention, that if the  FIR did not disclose the commission of an offence, the  court would be justified in quashing the proceedings  preventing the abuse of the process of law.
 Simultaneously, the courts are expected to adopt a
cautious approach in matters of quashing specially in  cases of matrimonial dispute whether the FIR in fact  discloses commission of an offence by the relatives of

the principal accused or the FIR prima facie discloses a  case of over-implication by involving the entire family  of the accused at the instance of the complainant, who  is out to settle her scores arising out of the teething  problem or skirmish of domestic bickering while  settling down in her new matrimonial surrounding.
15. Applying aforesaid principles of law to the facts of case and statements of witnesses, it is evident that a stereo type and omnibus allegations are employed against the applicants.
Apparently, this is a case of over implication whereby all the family members from husbands side are implicated.

The applicant no.7 resides at Dombivali (E), Tq. &
Dist. Thane and applicant no.6 who is husband's maternal uncle resides at Sadawan Bk., Tq. Amalner.
Applicant no.4 is sister-in-law of informant and resides with applicant no.5 at Dhule, applicant no.5 is husband of sister-in-law, they are residing at Datta Nagar, in Dhule City.
Further there are no specific allegations against respondent nos.2 and 3.

In the result, case is made out to exercise inherent powers under section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
